$comment: Module J v1.0, the Weyos baseline instrument, from the Chris McPherson advisory pack (2026-09-01): weyos-baseline-questionnaire.html, weyos-chris-walkthrough.html and Weyos_Chris_Worked_Example.xlsx. This file IS the scoring model. Code interprets it; code contains no weights. Bump instrument_version when a question or a weight changes: stored answers are re-scorable, and the version says which model scored them. Trait scores are internal and never reach a user-facing screen (SCRUM-91). Two resolutions in this file need sign-off from the pack's author: J1 feeds both T3 and T5 (the source formulas reference J1a/J1b, which the instrument does not have), and J3 is inverted in T2 but not in T4.

items.question: Which is closest to how your appetite usually works?
options: I can easily skip meals without noticing. I feel heavy after eating.
Fairly relaxed about food. Rarely urgent.
Middle of the road.
I notice hunger clearly and prefer to eat on time.
Strong, sharp appetite. I get irritable if a meal is delayed.

items.question: When you go to bed, what usually happens?
options: My mind is active and it takes a while to switch off.
Sometimes takes a while.
Varies.
Usually asleep fairly quickly.
I fall asleep quickly and sleep deeply.

items.question: How do you feel in the first hour after waking?
items.low: Groggy — I need a long runway

items.question: How would people describe the way you think and talk?
options: Measured and deliberate. I take time.
Fairly steady.
Depends on the situation.
Fairly quick and direct.
Fast, direct, straight to the point.

items.question: Do you run warm or cool compared to people around you?
Which best describes your energy through a typical day?
options: Comes in bursts and drops off suddenly. Unpredictable.
Somewhat variable.
Middle.
Fairly steady once I get going.
Slow to start, then steady all day.

items.question: Is there a time of day your energy reliably drops?
items.$comment: Unscored. Goes to the scheduler as the hour never to put a demanding action in.

items.question: When you're under real pressure, what's your first move?
options: I go quiet and pull back.
I internalise it and work through it alone.
Depends who's involved.
I get direct and push for a resolution.
I confront it head-on, sometimes sharply.

items.question: How predictable is your body's routine — sleep, appetite, digestion?
items.low: Varies a lot day to day

items.question: After a hard day, how long do you need to feel yourself again?
How do your joints and movement feel most days?
items.$comment: Answered and stored, but carries no weight in v1.0: the pack marks it as a weak T6 term with no weight given. Weight it here when the author supplies one.

scoring.$comment: Each answer is 1–5. An inverted term uses 6 − answer. Weights on an axis sum to 1, so the weighted answer is 1–5 and normalise(x) = (x − 1) / 4 × 100.

confidence.$comment: The engine only personalises on a trait whose confidence clears the gate. Self-report at signup does not, so on day one the product uses population defaults, and the description is shown only because a description is not a recommendation.

description.$comment: A trait produces a sentence only outside the middle band; a middling score says nothing worth saying. The most distinctive traits are read back, in trait order, up to max_fragments.

T1.low: You need a runway in the morning before you're really operating.
T1.high: You're up and functioning almost straight away.

T2.low: Your energy comes in bursts — strong, then it drops.
T2.high: You're steady all day once you're moving.

T3.low: You run cool and your appetite is easygoing.
T3.high: You run warm, and a delayed meal genuinely affects you.

T4.low: Under pressure you tend to go quiet and work it through yourself.
T4.high: Under pressure you get direct and push for a resolution.

T5.low: Your rhythm varies a lot day to day at the moment.
T5.high: Your body keeps a regular rhythm.

T6.low: You need real recovery time after a heavy day.
T6.high: You bounce back quickly from a hard day.

pairs.text: You're a slow starter who runs steady once you're going.
pairs.$comment: Two fragments collapse into one line because they say the same thing twice. Added in the worked example, not in the source spec: needs the author's confirmation.
